newsitem.title: FRANCE: French private pensions seen mainly drawing young.
newsitem.headline: French private pensions seen mainly drawing young.

text.p: People who take advantage of legislation allowing private pensions in France would have to start paying early in their careers to secure a sizeable retirement payout at 60, computer simulations by state-owned insurer CNP (Caisse Nationale de Prevoyance) show.

One simulation says a person contributing 800 francs a month from the age of 20 would secure monthly payouts of 5,712 francs on top of the maximum 20 percent lump sump withdrawal allowed by the private pensions law, recently adopted in parliament.

The same contribution would secure 3,077 francs a month for contributions started at the age of 30, 1,533 francs for those subscribing from age 40 and 576 francs a month for people who started paying in from the age of 50, it shows.

Many experts believe the option of voluntarily subscribing to a private pension fund alongside the current social security and mandatory top-up schemes will appeal mainly to those aged under 40 and that life assurance contracts, already popular, will prove more competitive for those aged 50 and over.
But CNP pension funds director Yannick Philippon told Reuters that the private pensions system could nevertheless prove attractive to people over 50 if they were paying high level contributions.

One of the main issues, he said, was creating a greater awareness of retirement benefit problems and winning over a public accustomed to life assurance contracts which provide big lump-sum payouts rather than annuities.
"It's true that there are a number of products such as life assurance which have got the French people used to near-total liquidity and availability of their capital," Philippon said.
The market for private pension funds could kick off at five billion francs in funds collected in its first year, rising only gradually thereafter, he said.
According to the CNP , a person contributing 1,000 francs a month from the age of 20 would secure 7,140 francs a month.
The same contribution would generate 3,847 francs a month if started at age 30, 1,916 francs for those starting at 40 and 720 francs starting a 50 years of age.
The simulation at this level is not directly comparable with that at 800 francs a month because it does not assume a 20 percent lump sum payout on retirement.

The simulationn also does not take account of additional employer contributions on an employee's behalf. The law allows employers to pay up to four times an employee's contribution and certain tax and payroll charge relief for employer payments.
Most sector experts believe people would contribute between 600 and 800 francs a month and that employers would top this up to the tune of 400 francs a month.
The pensions law was adopted in February, and decrees needed before private funds can start operating are expected to be issued in the coming months.
